clue.text: Poor little lamb!

parts.note: little, as in a small amount, means not much
a chop is a cut of lamb from the butcher

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a small sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an exclamation of pity for a lamb; in fact 'Poor' is the definition and 'little lamb' builds the phrase. NOT MUCH CHOP is Australian and British slang for no good.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase describes something of low quality or worthless, which is what poor means here.

clue.text: How fantastic to be out and about

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning, as in a business letter

explanation.surface: Someone remarks how marvellous it is to be out and about.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre is a borrowing from French for something bizarre or beyond the bounds of convention, so outlandish or fantastic.

clue.text: The least skimpy skirt is given to Mother

parts.note: a miniskirt, or mini, is a very short skirt
mum is an everyday British word for mother

explanation.surface: A daughter hands her mother the briefest of short skirts.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest possible amount is the bottom limit, the lowest quantity allowed.

clue.text: Young lad in the motor trade needs a lot of bottle

definitions.text: Young lad in the motor trade
definitions.meaning: a youngster working with automobiles could be called a ...
a large glass vessel for holding acids or other liquids, often in a wicker frame

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the word splits into an automobile plus a youth; as a single word it names a big, bulbous container for liquids.

clue.text: To applaud gin makes nonsense

parts.note: to clap is to applaud with the hands
a gin is also a snare or trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: Clapping for gin is a silly thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink, but it is the old word for a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means pretentious, empty talk meant to win applause, so rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: A Roman's involved in a row

indicators.note: involved means mixed up or entangled, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Roman citizen gets drawn into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' tells you to rearrange the letters of A ROMANS. 'row' looks like a quarrel but is the rowing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower is one of a crew who sits pulling an oar in a row of seats in a boat.

clue.text: He sees to it that a man's got aid or is rehabilitated

definitions.text: He sees to it that a man's got aid or is rehabilitated

indicators.note: to be rehabilitated is to be restored and reformed, so the letters before it are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A helper ensures a man in trouble receives assistance or is restored to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rehabilitated' shuffles A MANS GOT AID OR; the whole clue also describes the biblical stranger who helped the robbed traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The parable figure is the passer-by who stopped to help a beaten traveller, so anyone who helps someone in need.

clue.text: Make more bowlers take up position there

definitions.meaning: to make more of something is to raise its amount
in cricket, a bowler delivers from the crease, the line marked at each end of the pitch

explanation.definitionFit: To augment something is to add to it; split as two words it says where a cricket bowler stands, the crease being the white line by the stumps.

clue.text: How Cassius looked when he was faring badly?

definitions.text: How Cassius looked when he was faring badly?

parts.words: How Cassius looked when he was faring badly?
parts.note: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar says Cassius has a thin, starved look; faring badly is read as eating poorly

explanation.surface: A question about the appearance of the Roman conspirator Cassius when things were going badly for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faring badly' seems to mean doing poorly in life, but fare is also food: a man poorly fed looks thin and ravenous, as Caesar says of Cassius.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's line describes a thin, ravenous appearance, which is what a poorly fed man would show.

clue.text: Not infrequently decimal

definitions.meaning: something happening not infrequently happens many times

explanation.definitionFit: Frequently means many times; and a decimal system is one made up of tens, split as two words.

clue.text: Put in another order to get back the cooker

parts.note: rear means the back of something
a range is a large kitchen stove or cooker

explanation.surface: A cook orders a new stove and has to fetch it from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: A RANGE is a large old-fashioned kitchen stove, often built into a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: To place things in a different sequence is to sort them again in a new way.

clue.text: What the aspiring yacht-owner may do? Wow!

definitions.text: What the aspiring yacht-owner may do?
definitions.meaning: someone longing for a yacht can only fantasise about a vessel
an exclamation at the sight of a very attractive person

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word describes fantasising about a vessel; whole, it is slang for a strikingly attractive person who makes you exclaim.

clue.text: Medical man takes Ronald for a fool

parts.note: MO is short for medical officer, an army doctor
Ron is the short form of the name Ronald

explanation.surface: A doctor decides his patient Ronald is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an insult for a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Did they alert Capone to take weapons?

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: A question whether the police were warned when Al Capone went off to collect his guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Warning signals such as bells and sirens are what rouse people to danger.

clue.text: Order Ned a beer in Scotland

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters that follow are placed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend to buy Ned a pint while they are in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like asking the barman, but it tells you to rearrange NED A BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: The granite city on Scotland's north-east coast is a place in that country.

clue.text: A man in it reorganised support

indicators.note: reorganised means arranged differently, so the letters before it are shuffled

explanation.surface: An organisation gets a new man brought in to prop it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganised' tells you to rearrange the letters of A MAN IN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something going or uphold it is to back or prop it up.

clue.text: The type to give an impudent look

definitions.meaning: in printing, a heavy, thick typeface
a brazen, cheeky expression, a face showing boldness

explanation.definitionFit: Printers call heavy lettering by this name; read as two words it is a cheeky, brazen expression.

clue.text: A biblical translation prove-king strong hostility

parts.note: a version of the Bible, such as the Authorised Version, is a translation of it

explanation.surface: A new translation of the Bible stirs up bitter opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Authorised Version (King James Bible) is the classic English translation; 'prove-king' as filed is an OCR slip for 'provoking', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep dislike or antipathy is a strong feeling of being against something.

clue.text: Where rail passengers may be left standing

definitions.text: Where rail passengers may be left standing

parts.words: Where rail passengers may be left standing
parts.note: travellers waiting on a platform for a train that has gone, stranded where trains stop

explanation.surface: Commuters stranded without a seat or a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left standing' suggests a crowded carriage with no seats, but it means stranded on the platform after the train has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The stopping place for trains is where travellers wait, and may be left behind.

clue.text: Part of the rifle set right into the wood

indicators.note: into says the letter for right is set inside the word for the wood

parts.note: beech is a type of tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A gunsmith fits part of a rifle into a wooden stock.
explanation.definitionFit: On a gun, the rear of the barrel where the cartridge is loaded is a key component.

clue.text: It earns exchange currency for the Greek wine-trade

definitions.text: It earns exchange currency for the Greek wine-trade

indicators.note: exchange means swap around, so the letters of the two words before it are traded into new places

explanation.surface: A product brings in foreign money for Greece's vintners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges IT EARNS; the whole clue says this resinated wine brings foreign currency to Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The resin-flavoured white wine of Greece is a major export product of its vintners.

clue.text: Do take a drink, even if it causes trouble

parts.note: to do, as in to perform, is to act
to sup is to sip or drink

explanation.surface: Advice to have a drink, even though it might lead to bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To misbehave or malfunction is to give trouble, like a child or a faulty machine.

clue.text: Country in which the main dialects are Hindi

indicators.note: in which says the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A geography fact: the chief language of a nation is Hindi.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Asian nation where Hindi is the chief language is a country.

clue.text: Last month half Athens and London viewed a rigorous athletic contest

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the year's final month

indicators.note: half applies to both city names, taking the first half of each

explanation.surface: Last December, people watched a tough sporting event shared by two capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: The ten-event track and field competition is a gruelling sporting contest.

clue.text: Large number ensnared by enticement to make money

indicators.note: ensnared by means caught inside, so the number letter sits inside the word for enticement

parts.note: a lure is an enticement or bait
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted into a big money-making scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is money, especially when gained dishonourably.

clue.text: The people dealing in cameras

indicators.note: dealing, as with cards, suggests the letters are dealt out and shuffled

explanation.surface: A nation of photography traders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing' looks like trading but tells you to rearrange IN CAMERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The citizens of the United States are a nation, a people.

clue.text: Become liable to giving the mongrel a brusque command to enter

parts.note: a curt order telling someone to come inside is just in
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone sharply orders a scruffy dog indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something on yourself, such as costs or blame, is to become subject to it.

clue.text: Where Atlantic fishermen may be experiencing difficulties

definitions.text: Where Atlantic fishermen may be experiencing difficulties

parts.words: Where Atlantic fishermen may be experiencing difficulties
parts.note: ocean fishermen work far out over a great depth of sea, and the idiom for being in trouble describes the same place

explanation.surface: Trawlermen in the Atlantic run into problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Literally the deep-sea fishing grounds; idiomatically, being in serious trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being in serious trouble, and literally describes fishing over a great depth of ocean.
